articleTitle: Distance protection in a six-terminal transmission line: application review
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The fast and evolving power system requires low-cost solutions for the integration of new renewable sources. Six-terminal transmission or distribution lines are becoming an attractive option to allow the connection of solar and wind farms as it could overcome the limitation to build new lines and substations. These schemes could be also used to supply loads in high density areas or large industrial plants. Multi-terminal transmission lines create specific power protection challenges. In the past, the three-terminal line was considered the maximum number of terminals for reliable protection performance. Nowadays, line differential protection relays up to six-terminal makes this application more appealing as the unit scheme acts as the primary protection. Despite the availability of the 87L, the protection design should cater for the temporary or permanent loss of the line differential communication channel. Alternative sound protection methods should be available in the same relay. This paper reviews the challenges and possible solutions for the six-terminal scheme based on the distance protection, with and without communication available.

articleTitle: Hybrid travelling wave and ANN for fault location in branched distribution network
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The fault location in distribution network with multiple branches and mixed overhead lines and underground cable is of vital importance. A hybrid approach that combines Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and travelling wave based double-ended method in distribution network with multiple branches and mixed lines is investigated. An ANN is trained using limited amount of measurement to identify the faulty section in four terminals distribution network. Then, a double-ended traveling wave fault location is applied using terminals choice based on the ANN decision. The training data is generated using ATP-EMTP simulation software and the data processed using CWT to extract Time of Arrival (ToA) and analysed using MATLAB script. The analysis showed that the ANN is capable to identify fault section with accuracy of 90% or more while the fault location accuracy is within 99%. The algorithm is resilience to fault resistance, inception angle and fault types while it is influenced by the system added noise. However, analysing the recorded signal with multiple CWT levels enable the correct extraction of the fault wave arrival time.

articleTitle: New multi-ended fault-locating method utilizing incremental sequence quantities
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Accurate fault location of transmission line faults is crucial to make necessary repairs swiftly and reduce outage time. In this paper, a new multi-ended fault-locating method that uses pure-fault networks and incremental sequence quantities is presented. The proposed method uses time-synchronized voltage and current samples from all remote terminals, which makes this method suitable for integration in line current differential relays. Compared with the traditional multi-ended fault-locating method that solves faulted networks, this method provides better fault location estimates for untransposed lines. This paper demonstrates the accuracy of the proposed pure-fault network method by using simulations and field cases.

articleTitle: Utilizing high-quality waveform data to detect and diagnose protection misoperations and anomalies
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Power system protection is designed to rapidly clear faults with the aim of improving safety and reliability. While the protection system generally functions as intended, it does fail from time to time. Few oversight systems exist, however, to verify the proper operation of system protection, or help diagnose misoperations when they occur. Researchers at Texas A&M University have developed an automated waveform analytics system which, in addition to other functionality, allows utilities to quickly observe when protection anomalies occur, and obtain information to aid in post hoc investigations.

articleTitle: Open-source software for a fast and flexible implementation of an automated IEC 61850 engineering process
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Classical software products from vendors are restricted by technical and commercial boundary conditions that determines which features are provided to the customers at which point in time. The product management must find a compromise between limited development resources and a variety of feature wishes. Customer groups with special needs off the mainstream may be served not as quick on not as thorough as the bulk of customers with standard requirements. On the other hand, such software products tend to have a clearly defined feature set and a set price, which fits well with a classical procurement process. The maintenance is done by the vendor, the customer is a user only and bears only the responsibility of making the right choice. Open-Source Software follows a different approach. This may not match the conventional perception in electric power utilities of how to obtain a product or service. By involving themselves and becoming stakeholders in an Open-Source project, the stakeholders drive the developments into the direction they want. The stakeholders gain the authority to have features implemented they want to have, and the speed mostly depends on the intensity of the involvement, mainly the dedication of development resources. Besides focusing on one specific Open-Source Software solution for IEC 61850 engineering, this paper shall lay out the applicability and benefits of Open-Source concepts for Digital Substations.

articleTitle: Current-only fault passage indicator for high impedance grounded networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: In this paper a novel algorithm for earth-fault passage indication in high-impedance grounded medium voltage networks is proposed. Given that the majority of secondary substations in medium voltage (MV) grids lack voltage measurements, the algorithm relies solely on current measurements. This feature significantly reduces the time required to identify faulty sections, thereby accelerating power restoration for all affected customers. Unlike other current-only methods, the proposed approach eliminates the need for estimating any fundamental or higher harmonic phasors. It is also resilient to false indications that can occur during post-fault transients or from unreliable phasor information during steady-state conditions – issues often influenced by the level of network compensation. The proposed method achieves robust and accurate fault passage indications through the utilization of transient signal components in short time intervals following fault inception. The algorithm’s efficacy is validated using fault records from real-world power networks.

articleTitle: A novel real time laboratory test equipment for a network of travelling wave fault location devices
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: A novel laboratory test equipment was developed to test a network of travelling wave fault location (TWFL) devices for Svenska Kraftnät (SVK)’s Factory Acceptance Test (FAT). The FAT requires a combination of fault types and fault locations to be tested at different nodes on the cross-bonded cable network, together with their correct reporting to SCADA. There is no low-cost test system available which can simulate travelling wave signals in real-time on a wide-area network, under different operating and fault conditions. A flexible hardware real-time simulator was therefore developed for this purpose, which can validate the overall behaviour of TWFL systems from the simplest end-to-end circuits up to interconnected multi-bus wide area networks. The parameters required to execute this simulator are the precise arrival timing values of the incident and reflected signals at each node generated by a fault on the network, their polarities and the ‘pseudo’ RMS current values. This paper describes the SVK project which initiated this development. The features of the TWFL system are discussed, in particular its wide area fault location algorithm, which can be demonstrated effectively with this test equipment. The design of the test equipment is depicted in detail. Finally, the process of the SVK FAT is presented.

articleTitle: Emergency control measures against long term voltage instability
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: System collapse may be caused by undesired protection relay operations during voltage instability. In this paper, the analysis of different emergency control measures is presented as means to prevent voltage collapse when long term voltage instability is evolving in the system. Being the first line of defence after such unexpected relay trip, the emergency control of load tap changers (LTC) of power transformers during undervoltage conditions is investigated. Alternatively, load shedding is applied to avoid undesired Zone 3 distance relay trips. Sensitivities of Zone 3 trip margin to load powers are calculated to determine the most efficient load shedding actions to prevent undesired operation of critical relays. The effectiveness of the proposed emergency control measures is demonstrated though simulation results for the Hellenic Interconnected System model.

articleTitle: Find a better way: National Grid experience on circuit breaker fail replacement at mesh corner substation
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET) policy requires Circuit Breaker Fail (CBF) protection for 400kV and 275kV circuit breakers. CBF is provided to detect and interrupt any uncleared system faults due to a failure of the circuit breaker mechanism or a failure of the circuit breaker current interrupting device. When a fault occurs and a circuit breaker fails to clear the fault, it is necessary to trip all the circuit breakers beyond the faulty breaker to isolate the uncleared fault. NGET is facing a large volume of P&C asset replacement target in the RIIO T2 price control period, system access and resources are difficult to obtain, especially for mesh corner substations as one circuit breaker controls multiple circuits. Traditionally, the outage for secondary equipment intervention is tagged along with other work against primary equipment which requires longer outage. However, this has proven to be a challenge from a co-ordination of planning point of view. Also, the design needs to be staged depending on the outage availability. If the outage sequences are altered at any point during delivery, the design stages has to change according which is not cost effective and forces tremendous pressure on resources. Therefore, a new way of working has been considered in order to achieve accelerated delivery for this type of asset intervention. This paper introduces new design and commissioning strategy to deliver the Circuit Breaker Fail protection replacement for mesh corner substation. The focus will be on the protection design and installation, comparing two sites with different methodologies, and will try to overcome some of the challenges from the experience.

articleTitle: Current-only directional protection of distribution networks using low-cost communication
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Conventional distribution protection schemes may not be suitable for evolving and future networks due to the rapid increase in distributed energy resources. This paper presents a review of selected novel protection principles for distribution networks and proposes a new and effective protection technique using only current measurements, based upon comparison between pre- and during-fault current phasors. This comparison process only requires low-cost communication systems for intermittent data transmission between measurement points. An overview of potential communication solutions is also contained in the paper. The operation of the method is tested and validated using simulated case studies of different scenarios, which demonstrate that the proposed scheme is highly effective in detecting and isolating faults, thus presenting a promising solution for protection of future active distribution networks.

articleTitle: Coordination of requirements related to the insertion of renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The increasing number of Renewable Energy Resources connected via power converters to all voltage levels of the electrical network has given raise to concerns about the performance of the different protection functions and devices. Numerous publications have analysed this impact and investigated possible improvements or workarounds for the identified issues. In some of them, the possibility to limit the impact on the network protection by enforcing adequate requirements of the connecting converters has been discussed. Other similar technical issues exist on other domains, namely the impact on High Voltage Equipment. This paper gives an overview over the interdependency between these different issues and their relationship with regulation and standardisation.

articleTitle: Effects of system stray capacitances on overcurrent and directional traveling wave protections applied to lines near inverter-based resources
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper analyzes the effects of transformer and busbar stray capacitances on existing traveling wave (TW)-based overcurrent and directional protection elements (called TW50 and TW32, respectively), when applied to lines that interconnect inverter-based resources (IBRs). IBR-interconnecting transmission lines are usually terminated by transformers, which are seen as open circuits when high frequency components are analyzed. Thus, stray capacitances on the IBR-interconnecting line terminals dictate the shape of measured TWs, consisting in an important aspect for TW-based functions. PSCAD simulations are carried out to investigate the TW50 and TW32 protections, allowing to evaluate in the impacts of distortions and attenuations that take place on the measured wavefronts at both IBR and grid sides. The obtained results show that the system stray capacitances levels have an important effect on the performance of both TW50 and TW32 elements.

articleTitle: Standardisation of a merged process and station bus network
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The conceptualisation of IEC 61850 digital substations has typically treated station and process bus as distinct networks, with station bus for station supervisory and control functions, and process bus for bay level communications and interaction with primary equipment. It is possible to utilise Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP) and 1Gbps interfaces (where available) to merge the station and process bus onto the same physical network, while maintaining functional separation. This paper outlines the drivers behind merging the two buses, feasibility studies that were carried out, positive design implications, and the practical realities of implementation with current market devices.

articleTitle: Ultra-high speed transmission line protection performance in time domain due to several contingency situations
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper will approach the use of a system composed by software and hardware capable of accurate modeling all components of the electrical system, including transmission lines (models with variable and frequency-dependent parameters), and reproducing the wave forms up to megahertz on secondary levels. It will be demonstrated the performance of an ultra-high-speed transmission line protection that works in time domain using incremental magnitudes and is based on the principles of traveling waves (TW) to identify and locate a fault. So, an IED will be submitted to hundreds of contingency situations in order to evaluate the performance of protection function based on traveling waves based on the following parameters: correct fault location (errors of at most the transmission tower span length) and protection function delay (values around 1ms). It will also be possible to compare the performance of protection system based on TW with the traditional function based on impedance calculation.

articleTitle: Protection of harmonic filter banks
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Power quality is an important consideration for grid operators and large industrial power users who face different network challenges. Grid operators are challenged with minimizing losses over long transmission lines, integrating renewable generation (e.g., wind, solar) and providing voltage support during unplanned network events are critical in delivering efficient and reliable grids. Large industrial power consumers face the challenge of lower operating costs as well as meeting contractual conditions related to power factor and harmonic distortion to secure electrical supply. HV harmonic filter banks are then often used in order to remove harmonics from the modern power network. This paper describes protection principles and schemes which can be applied on such HV harmonic filter banks, as well as provide guidance to protection engineers.

articleTitle: Performance of compensation relays with inverted based resources
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The concept of compensation relays has been used for a long time in transmission line distance protection. Compensation relays use the relationship between sequence voltages at the zone boundary to distinguish between internal and external faults. In the traditional power system, when the system connected in two-line terminals can be modelled as synchronous generators, compensation relays work as expected. However, the effectiveness of compensation relays deteriorates when inverter-based resources (IBR) are connected to the transmission line terminal. The impact of IBR on compensation relays is described in thi s paper. Type 3, Type 4, and solar PV IBR are considered in the study for demonstrating the challenges. Different fault scenarios are considered to explain the problem. Additionally, the impact of sampling frequency in those scenarios is also presented in the paper. It can be concluded that compensation relays face problems when connected with IBR with phase-phase faults causing the worst-case scenario.

articleTitle: The optimum mother wavelet for travelling wave fault locators
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Research into travelling waves used for fault location mainly utilize digital transient models of the power system under fault conditions. Electromagnetic transient analysis is the foundation for travelling wave-based fault location estimation, and when they are applied with precise time synchronization, extremely high accuracy is achieved. Most travelling wave-based fault locators detect the time of arrivals of the fault incident surges at both ends of a transmission line, and this requires a level of time precision compatible with the speed of light. Fault signals are non-stationary and non-periodic, and consequently, an important tool to provide multiresolution analysis of the fault signals is the wavelet transform. Wavelets from Daubechies family are normally recommended by researchers that studied faults generated by electromagnetic simulators. However, the real-world travelling wave fault data described in this paper was obtained from the recording of the actual faults on transmission lines; using synchronized fault locators positioned at both ends of various transmission lines. With decomposition and reconstruction of signals at the scaling level of up to six, this paper provides a thorough comparison between the Daubechies, Biorthogonal, Symlet and Coiflet wavelet families, and underlines their accuracy and reliability for use in fault location analysis.

articleTitle: Impact of converter equivalent impedance on distance protection with the MHO characteristic
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: With the rapid increase of Converter-Based Resources (CBRs) and the decommission of conventional Synchronous Generators (SGs), recent studies have found that distance protection can face significant challenges. One of the key factors that can impact the protection performance is the CBRs’ fault behaviour being different from SGs, leading to the different characteristics of their equivalent internal impedance, which will have a particular impact on distance protection with the memory-polarised Mho characteristic. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of the characteristics of the equivalent internal impedance of CBRs with different control strategies, based on which, their impact on the memory-polarised Mho distance protection is analysed in detail. In the paper, the equivalent impedance of CBRs with virtual impedance-based Grid Forming Control (GFM) and balanced current injection-based Grid Following Control (GFL) are calculated and plotted against time throughout the faults. These are then compared with the internal impedance of a reference voltage source. It is found that, unlike the SGs, which can be considered as voltage sources and have constant source impedance, CBRs’ internal impedance have dynamic and time-varying characteristics, which are governed by the implemented Fault-Ride-Through (FRT) control strategies. Such characteristics will lead to dynamical changes in the expansion levels of the Mho protection zones, which could lead to increase risks of protection failure and/or maloperation. It is also revealed that, by better understanding the internal impedance characteristics of CBRs, the control strategies of CBRs could potentially be refined to mitigate the negative impact on Mho distance operation, thus presenting a potential solution to mitigate the risks of compromised performance of memory-polarised Mho distance protection.

articleTitle: Optimizing underfrequency load shedding strategies in converter-dominated networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy resources into the power grid has introduced challenging problems that need to be overcome to ensure system stability and reliability. This paper applied an Integrated Protection-Planning Simulation (IPPS) technology to evaluate an innovative Underfrequency Load Shedding (UFLS) scheme with the objective of complying with NERC Standard PRC-006-5 considering penetration of Inverter-Based Resources (IBR). IPPS technology creates a simulation platform that allows the modeling of highly detailed protection models in transient stability analysis. This paper took advantage of the new features enabled by IPPS and modeled a novel UFLS relay logic with Rate-of-Change-of-Frequency (RoCoF) supervision. The RoCoF-supervised UFLS has the advantage of avoiding misoperation at industrial motor loads and allowing for reduced UFLS time delay. A sudden loss of generation condition was simulated in IPPS according to the PRC-006-5 standard requirements. The protection logic of both the conventional UFLS program and the RoCoF-supervised UFLS scheme have been examined by incrementally increasing the IBR penetration level. The IPPS tool provided accurate simulation results including frequency profile and Volts per Hertz values at all generation buses. The performance of the novel UFLS scheme has been compared with the conventional scheme to validate its effectiveness. An automatic load restoration scheme to prevent frequency overshoot after UFLS occurs has also been implemented along with the addition of a Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to provide fast frequency response and further alleviate system-wide frequency decay.

articleTitle: Time-domain fault location method for medium voltage cables using sheath currents
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for real-time fault location in medium voltage (MV) cables, for single-phase to ground faults. The method is based on the sheath currents. By utilizing instantaneous measurements of voltage and current at the cable’s sending end, the voltages and currents of the sheaths at the receiving end are computed. A criterion is then introduced, relying on the calculated receiving end of the cable sheaths voltages and current. This approach offers two advantages: it operates in the time-domain which minimizes phasor calculation error, and it doesn’t require real-time communication. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated through 1080 transient simulations in MATLAB/Simulink, yielding fault location estimates within 40ms and a maximum error of 0.26%. Furthermore, the proposed method is relatively unaffected by distorted voltage and current waveforms due to its reliance on time-domain analysis.

articleTitle: Understanding the impacts of networks and parallel redundancy protocol for process bus applications
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: In a digital substation, process bus (PB) refers to a local-area communication network used to interface critical information, such as sampled values and trip signals, between primary equipment and protection and control devices. To improve protection system reliability of a digital substation, an engineered network is required for the PB. An ideal PB network must be robust and resilient. Robustness can be achieved by characterization of the network path, such as latency, packet delay variation (PDV) also known as jitter, packet loss rates, and bandwidth usage. Resiliency is usually achieved by incorporating redundancy or duplication. Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP) is a natural choice for PB, especially for transmission substations; however, redundancy can be ineffective if not constantly supervised and will hide failures in plain sight. In this paper, we outline a method for achieving robustness and resilience by closely analyzing PB network characteristics. We also discuss safe deployment of redundancy using PRP technology on PB applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of SRF-PLL sensitivity to voltage waveform distortions due to harmonics
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of voltage waveform distortions, caused by harmonics, on a widely utilized single-phase synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL). It defines groups of test waveforms (TWs), based on the harmonic components and magnitudes recommended by the IEC 61000-4-13 standard, with phase angles determined through a genetic algorithm (GA). This method identifies TWs featuring the most significantly shifted zero-crossings (ZCs), the highest/lowest peak values (PVs), various counts of ZCs, and step-change ZC shifts with multiple ZCs (MZCs). Additionally, an analytical method for defining worst-case ZC-shifted TWs is presented. In line with the IEEE C37.118 standard recommendations, several error indices are employed to evaluate the impact of the TWs on the SRF-PLL model. These indices include magnitude error (ME), phase angle error (PE), total vector error (TVE), frequency error (FE), and rate of change of frequency error (RFE). Th e results presented demonstrate complex sensitivity patterns, which should aid PLL designers in better evaluating the performance of SRF-PLLs under harmonic distortions in supply voltage waveforms, thereby improving their operation and reducing related errors. The analysis also contributes to specifying more comprehensive test methods and TWs for assessing and benchmarking the performance of PLLs and other synchrophasor measurement devices.

articleTitle: Development of protection and control system complying with IEC 61850
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: In recent years, fully digital substation systems complying with the IEC 61850 standard at the station bus and process bus levels have been applied worldwide. Discussion of the application and practical use as well as development of process bus-based systems have been progressing in Japan. Tokyo Electric Power Co. Power Grid has applied its first process bus-based system at the Chiba Inzai 275kV substation. The IEC 61850 standard is applied in Process Interface Units (PIUs) and process level communication is digitalized with Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs). We evaluated and took measures using a failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA) method to ensure system reliability. We also considered environmental withstand in terms of impulse voltage which would affect PIUs installed closed to the switchgear. Satisfactory tests results were obtained through type test of each requirement.

articleTitle: Impact of a power converter virtual impedance based fast fault current injection control strategy on distance protection
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: An increasing trend in the power system involves the substitution of conventional power units with Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). The fault response characteristics of VSCs are mainly determined by the current rating of its semiconductor device and the control strategy applied to them, which cannot inherently generate a large amount of fault current like traditional synchronous generators. Moreover, with the suppression of negative sequence current under unbalanced conditions, VSCs will affect the apparent impedance seen by the distance relay, thus affecting the distance protection of transmission lines. This paper investigates a Fast Fault Current Injection -Virtual Converter System (FFCI-VCS) control strategy based on a virtual impedance network, which serves two pivotal objectives: firstly, to enable the converter to inject the maximum feasible fault current during the initial 1-2 cycles subsequent to a grid fault event, and secondly, to enhance the operational efficiency of distance protection systems. The performance of the FFCI-VCS is evaluated through Simulink simulations under both balanced and unbalanced grid faults. The outcomes verify its ability to achieve fast fault current injection and diminish the response time of distance relays across various fault types, transmission distances, and fault resistance conditions.

articleTitle: Contrasting the requirements on MMC control for grid code compliance and distance protection
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The reduction in synchronous generation and the increase in power-electronic interfaced renewable resources and HVDC links are causing significant challenges to distance protection schemes, including incorrect zone selection, phase selection, or functional directional elements. At the same time, current existing grid codes require converters to inject reactive current during AC-side faults to support the grid voltage. In existing literature, these two topics are investigated separately. However, the contrast between these two requirements has not been studied. In this paper, we contrast the requirements originating from the grid code and distance protection on converter control. First, the critical control parameters that affect the two sets of requirements are identified using sensitivity analysis. Second, the impacts of the identified critical parameters on the two sets of requirements are examined for time domain simulations with the aim of investigating whether there are conflicts between these two control objectives. The research indicates that increasing fault current injection droop and the ratio of AC-side power used for total energy control leads to a greater margin for grid code compliance while yielding adverse consequences for distance protection.

articleTitle: Fault detection and location in floating windfarms with fishbone inter-array architecture
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This article focuses on the development of a traveling wave-based protection strategy to enhance the fault-locating capabilities of the array grid’s protection system. Initially, a PSCAD simulation model is employed to model a floating wind farm with fishbone inter-array architecture, encompassing components such as transmission cables, transformers, wind turbine generators, and grid connections. These models are tailored to align with traveling wave theory. The article primary objective is to devise a protection strategy capable of accurately detecting and locating faults within the array grid. The analysis demonstrates that Haar and Daubechies 2 mother wavelets, employed in wavelet transform, exhibit exceptional time-frequency analysis properties, enabling the detection of traveling wave arrivals. Furthermore, when extending the double-ended fault locating method to a multiterminal system, the wavelet transform emerges as a reliable input for identifying faults within the fishbone inter-array grid. The effectiveness of the traveling wave-based fault protection strategy is evaluated through various study cases involving different fault types, locations, and inception angles. The analysis underscores the strategy's sensitivity to voltage traveling waves, with zero voltage inception angle faults posing a detection challenge. Nonetheless, overall, the traveling wave-based fault protection strategy exhibits strong performance in fault localization.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a transient current protection algorithm based on Kalman filter residual
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This manuscript describes a novel pilot protection algorithm specifically designed for two and three-terminal transmission lines, centred on protecting transmission lines using the Kalman filter residual (KFR) . It presents the fundamental operating principle of the proposed method and its practical implementation, offering a straightforward and detailed account of its functionality. Furthermore, the manuscript discusses the hardware requirements necessary for deploying the proposed algorithm, providing a clear understanding of the infrastructure demands. Additionally, the manuscript features a comprehensive examination of two actual disturbances, showcasing the responses of the proposed algorithm to both scenarios. The results indicate that the algorithm is accurate, secure, dependable, and fast in fault detection and isolation. This research serves as a valuable contribution to the domain of power system protection, offering a practical solution for transmission lines that meets the high standards of performance demanded by the power industry.

articleTitle: Impact on breaker failure protection by using non-conventional transducers
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents the study results on using non-conventional transducer outputs for breaker failure protection (BFP) functions. The paper starts with modelling of non-conventional transducers according to IEC 61869 standards by applying both analogue and digital integration methods. A basic description of BFP is then provided. A test model which includes both the primary power system and the BFP function is built in PSCAD which mimics the actual BFP function used in industry. The verification is carried by applying different faults which are inputs for non-conventional transducers, and the output of the transducers is connected to BFP function. In order to confirm the results, a protection relay configured with BFP function is tested in a hardware-in-loop configuration by running the recorded files from PSCAD model in real-time and feeding its output to the process bus interface of the relay. In both conditions, it is noticed that the BFP might trip incorrectly during switch off faults due to the longer decaying tail of transducer output if the model is just following the design demand on IEC 61869 standards with 1 Hz cut-off frequency limits regarding DC component suppression. Finally, the conclusions are given with suggested actions both in standard aspects and test aspects under digital substation environment.

articleTitle: Impact of weather on cable insulation monitoring of the UK railway signalling power distribution network
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The UK railway signalling power system employs an IT configuration to ensure uninterrupted power supply and minimize operational disruptions. This paper explores the impact of weather on cable insulation monitoring by analysing insulation monitoring data from multiple UK railway networks alongside historical weather data. Relative humidity and precipitation are identified as key influencers of insulation variations, meaning that normalizing data for these factors is crucial when evaluating cable insulation conditions. Additionally, the study also emphasises the need to account for changes in signal propagation velocity for TDR-based monitoring technologies. These insights underscore the importance of accounting for weather effects, enhancing the reliability and precision of cable insulation monitoring in electrical systems.

articleTitle: Transient current curves characteristics based MMC-HVDC line breakage protection
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: When a line breakage fault occurs in the MMC-HVDC, there is a risk of instability in the DC voltage at the fault pole, and it is necessary to quickly identify the breakage section and switch the MMC control to maintain the voltage stability. However, the existing line breakage protection is not mature, so a novel line breakage protection with the characteristics of the current fitting curve is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the characteristics of the electrical quantity change after line breakage fault are analysed. Theoretically, DC voltage is destabilized, and DC current oscillates and decays to zero. Then, the distribution characteristics of the extreme point of the fault current fitting curve are used to judge the internal breakage fault. Finally, a true bipolar system is constructed in PSCAD to verify the performance of the proposed line breakage protection. The proposed protection principle is simple, fast, and accurate in determining the internal breakage section and has an excellent anti-noise performance.

articleTitle: Assessing the performance of an enhanced distance relay in converter-dominated network
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Converter-dominated networks (CDN) not only limits the fault current, but also results in different fault current signatures with respect to what is typically observed during a fault with conventional generation. Major research activities across the globe (SANDIA and MIGRATE projects) have raised concerns that the commercially available distance relays are not reliable and could misoperate in the presence of inverter based resource(IBR). This paper evaluates the performance of the protective relay with an enhanced distance algorithm (phase selection, distance characteristics and directional) from multiple dimensions i.e., speed, selectivity, security, stability and dependability. The performance evaluation is done using COMTRADES obtained from electromagnetic transient program (EMTP) which incorporates ''Real Controller'' IBR Type - III onshore wind turbine and battery energy storage models considering different fault location, fault type, fault resistance, point-on-wave, operating scenarios and IBR penetration levels including 100% renewable generation. Investigation shows that the enhanced distance algorithm provides promising performance in CDN.

articleTitle: Behaviour analysis of transmission line protection functions in grids with high penetration of renewable sources
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an assessment of the potential impact of the high penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) on the protection functions for transmission lines. The performed analysis was done on a simulation model of part of a transmission grid with wind farms (WFs) connected to various substations. A dynamic model was used for the wind generators, including fault-ride-though capability and reactive power contribution during faults. Faults were simulated to obtain graphs of (i) short-circuit currents feeding faults and (ii) measurement of apparent impedance seen by a distance protection in relation to the corresponding Mho circles. The analysis of these elements was then used to assess the behaviour of the protection functions . Results show that the magnitude of current contributions coming from generation points considerably decreases when comparing the use of traditional Synchronous Generators (SGs) and WFs. In addition, it was seen that apparent impedance measurements don’t suffer distortion regarding the generator’s technology and, therefore, the behaviour and response of distance protections in transmission lines remains valid and a correct tripping command would be issued. Further research might include the use of Hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) with protection relays from different vendors and the interaction with more complex and realistic transmission grids.

articleTitle: Rapid inetia emulation control through supercapacitor considering internal resistance
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: A rapid inertia emulation control (INEC) from renewable power generation is crucial to strengthen power system frequency stability, especially initial rate of change of frequency, during grid contingencies. Supercapacitor (SC) is a promising energy source for INEC, due to its high power density and long life cycle. However, SC may suffer from a slow response speed due to its relatively high internal resistance (IR), which is not well addressed in exsiting research. To solve this problem, this paper first investigates IR influence mechanism on SC INEC performance, and then proposes a novel control to compensate for SC IR voltage drop, such that a rapid INEC through SC is realized. The effectiveness of the proposed control in minimizing SC INEC response time and enhancing grid frequency stability is verified through simulation studies.

articleTitle: Dependability and performance analysis of redundant DSAS architectures using FEH and MRM
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Digital substation (DS) is an integral part of the smart grid migration plan. Availability/reliability of DS has been evaluated using traditional approaches. Although many new methods have been proposed, there is no standard approach exist till date. Due to evolving cyber-physical nature of Digital Substation Automation System (DSAS), this paper investigates the effect of inclusion of Fault/Error Handling Model (FEH) on the availability of three redundant DSAS architectures by comparing it with the conventional Reliability Block Diagram (RBD) models. The paper also discusses the need to include Markov reward process (MRP) based performance model into dependability analysis of DSAS and demonstrates its effect on the dependability of DSAS through both, analytical and simulation methods.

articleTitle: Design considerations of implementing process bus and PTP along an IEC 61850-based main line traction power system
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: In the realm of modern energy systems, the deployment of advanced technologies is reshaping the way power grids are monitored and managed. The IEC 61850 suite of standards has emerged as a key player in enhancing communications and interoperability within substations, enabling efficient data exchange and control. This paper outlines the design considerations when implementing and piloting advanced IEC 61850 monitoring and file collection capabilities in a system using Sampled Values (SV) on a process bus and Manufacturing Message Specification (MMS) file services in a Network Rail substation on the Great Western Main Line (GWML). The objective of this advanced IEC 61850 monitoring and file collection system is to independently manage, process, and act upon measurements and fault information retrieved from substations and traction power infrastructure. This paper discusses the operational benefits derived from this trial project, the challenges faced when implementing these systems, and the remedial actions introduced to mitigate these challenges. Time synchronisation forms a critical component when implementing a process bus solution. This paper describes several architectures and deployment methods that must be considered when deploying Precision Time Protocol (PTP) across the network and it presents some of the issues identified during the implementation of the system. These challenges can be further exacerbated when considering both a larger network and intersubstation communications for protection and control applications. This paper further outlines the cybersecurity requirements that were fulfilled as part of the implementation.

articleTitle: Transient energy based directional detection for series compensated parallel lines
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a newly developed directional detection solution based on fault induced transient energy. The solution has been used for heavily series compensated parallel lines as directional units to enhance permissive overreach transfer tripping (POTT) scheme as the redundant protection function in actual 525 kV transmission networks. This paper starts with introduction of transient energy based directional detection method and advantages first. Then the paper describes the technical principle of the directional detection concept and proposes a new solution of transient energy direction detection suitable for series compensated line conditions. In order to verify the solution, site records and simulation tests have been used to verify the new solution. The actual site test example of POTT scheme based on the proposed solution is given further. Finally the conclusions are provided by confirming the performance of the new solution with both good dependability and security for series compensation protection application conditions.

articleTitle: Enhancing fault location on transmission lines by combining traveling wave-based functions available in real devices
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology to improve transmission line traveling wave (TW)-based fault location (TWFL) procedures by combining promptly available results obtained from classical single- and double-ended TWFL methods widely available in off-the-shelf devices. The goal is to reduce TWFL errors caused by uncertainties in line electrical parameters and two-terminal data time misalignment, without requiring time-consuming fault record inspections. Real and simulated fault records are analyzed to assess the methodology performance. Obtained results demonstrate the proposed solution is indeed able to reduce the impacts of time synchronization errors and uncertainties in line parameters, being attractive for TWFL computational platforms.

articleTitle: Machine learning-based anomaly detection methods to enhance cyber capability for electricity network protection and control
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Digital substations are enablers for the electricity network power flow to be controlled and directed safely and securely from generation to demand, these make them a highly attractive target for cyber-attackers aimed at disrupting operations. As a result, Protection, Automation and Control (PAC) devices will be required not only as business usual to maintain effective detection of network normal and fault conditions but also to detect anomaly cyber-attack conditions. This paper proposes an anomaly detection method based on time series data and a Back Propagation (BP) neural network algorithm. The BP neural network is used to classify the anomaly data via extracting anomaly system state behaviour characteristics and then comparing them with normal system states. By using the supervising training and learning process, an anomaly Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is developed and used to determine when and whether anomaly data would occur. A benchmark 4 bus power system used by ABB and a typical distribution network substation with 2 power source infeeders and 4 load feeders were selected and modelled using Digsilent Power Factory simulation tool to obtain different time series network condition data as inputs to the implemented IDS. Results show that the BP neural network can accurately detect all tested anomaly cyber-attack conditions and provide the correct system state. The comparison between the proposed method and ABB algorithm proposed Kirchhoff’s laws-based distributed agreement algorithm was made. By comparisons, the advantages and disadvantages of using the proposed method are discussed and highlighted.

articleTitle: Application of distance protection to offshore windfarm with external disturbance
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper analysed the challenges of the distance protection application at the AC windfarm offshore platform array cables and inter-tie cables. The study cases are based on fault records that were retrieved from an offshore windfarm in which Siemens Energy was the principal contractor. This paper focused on the distance protection stability for the fault ride through requirement of National Grid (NG). Also, during the offshore 66kV earth fault, the distance protection will be impacted by the unbalanced charging current flow due to the zero-sequence path resembling an isolated earth system. At end of this paper the protection logic improvements for this application are discussed.

articleTitle: Automating commissioning tests, firmware updates and inventory checks using a device management system
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The topic of IED lifecycle management concerns the processes for password management, firmware upgrades, configuration changes and the readjustment of Protection Settings, is of utmost importance to Utility Managers looking for optimum OPEX performance. This is because these processes (which often include site visits) can ordinarily take up a substantial amount of time, and therefore expenditure for their maintenance. This paper therefore looks at how Device Management techniques could be applied for each of these use cases, even including a commissioning assistant for automating on site testing. The main message of this paper is that the maintenance and management of installed devices could be industrialised by leveraging digitalised device management techniques to carry out these tasks in a secure, reliable, remote, and even batch processed manner.

articleTitle: A combination approach for fault location in MV distribution networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an earth fault location method tailored for medium voltage (MV) radial distribution networks. The proposed approach combines a zero-sequence impedance-based with additional measurements (ZSAM) technique and a modified Takagi (MT) method from previous works. This novel approach exploits the strengths of both methods and overcomes the challenge of multiple solutions inherent in the MT method while reducing the size of the solution area of the ZSAM method. By combining these techniques, the proposed method effectively converges the benefits of ZSAM and MT approaches, providing a small set of nodes as the solution for fault location.

articleTitle: Impact of grid connection requirements on protection systems in offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Installed capacity of Offshore Wind Farms (OWF) is growing rapidly as more countries all around the world aim either to expand the existing fleet or start using offshore wind resources to cover the ever-increasing demand for clean and affordable renewable energy. Meeting grid code requirements and ensuring compliance with other relevant standards and regulations is a cornerstone of successful deployment of OWFs and connection to the grid. However, understanding the grid connection requirements relevant to the protection systems scope is not that straightforward. The paper provides an overall concept of compliance and introduces typical groups of connection requirements specifically applicable to protection systems in OWFs. Impact of such requirements on protection systems design, testing, operation, and maintenance procedures as well as challenges associated with their fulfilment are discussed and supported by several examples. The paper also presents a roadmap to ensuring compliance with grid connection requirements. Information presented in the paper creates awareness among all the industry players and helps to overcome challenges associated with meeting connection requirements for OWFs.

articleTitle: Voltage transformer failure during routine switching in Drill Site
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: An extensive 34.5kV Drake overhead line network (OHL) supplies power to a group of Drill Sites scattered across a vast desert area. During routine energization in one of these sites, a bus-side voltage transformer experienced an insulation failure at the primary winding neutral point. This paper summarizes the frequency domain analysis to identify the root cause of the failure, as well as the phasor domain methodology to determine the parameter limits of the neutral voltage displacement (ANSI59) and negative sequence overvoltage (ANSI47) as protection functions against transient overvoltage conditions (TOV) and slow front transients (SFO) caused by switching, fault clearance or ferroresonance. As a lesson learned, installing an additional surge arrester at the main incomer, in addition to the one at the riser pole, must always be evaluated against ground faults close to the supply cable termination.

articleTitle: Recent policy developments in National Grid busbar protection application
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract:
During 2022, National Grid undertook a thorough review of its application policy for the busbar protection applied to its busbar type substations, chiefly at 275kV and above but also covering 132kV and below. This review, carried out at the request of th e Group Chief Engineer, re-examined busbar protection policy for the first time in twenty years and compared practices across its UK and US transmission networks. The review was concluded with the publication of an internal National Grid Technical Report and informed the recent revision of busbar protection application policy, outlined in the revised policy statement. This paper outlines the findings of the Technical Report and the justification behind recent policy changes within National Grid. These are summarised below:

Duplicated busbar protection systems on new build substations at 275kV and above

132kV and below specified on a case-by-case basis, subject to system criticality and station size

Duplicated distributed or process bus architecture required on asset replacement

Circuit-breaker fail protection to be housed in bay level hardware (external to the busbar protection) where possible

High impedance electromechanical technology is not precluded.

articleTitle: Diagnostic tool to monitor performance of inverter-based resource during network faults
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Failure to ride through faults or events and the modification of sequence components during faults by the control system of inverter-based resource (IBR) are matter of concern during network operations. Standards like IEEE-2800 address technical minimum requirements for IBR interconnecting with the transmission system (TS). We have developed a diagnostic tool to confirm if IBR performance is compliant with the IEEE-2800 standard. The tool monitors the line-to-line and line-to-ground voltages, positive and negative sequences of voltage and current, and active and reactive powers at the point of measurement. It assesses these quantities to determine mode of operation and current injection slops of IBR during network faults. In case of inadvertent tripping, the tool also provides root cause analysis and possible remedial actions like changing mode of operation, gain setting, etc. It also helps IBR owners to monitor PLL performance. Case studies are presented on test systems using PSCAD simulation. Some scenarios underscore the requirement of diagnostic tool.

articleTitle: Impacts of GFM inverters on legacy distance protection relays
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper analyzes the interactions between conventional Line Distance Protection (LDP) relays and Grid-Forming (GFM) inverters. Various fault types, arc resistances and locations were investigated in a PSCAD model consisting of either a Synchronous Generator (SG) or a GFM inverter connected to the utility grid by a transformer and two transmission lines. A simple distance relay algorithm was coded in Matlab, tuned for the SG and then analyzed together with data obtained from the same system but using a GFM inverter instead. It is found that the inverter can make the relays able to trip correctly for many zone 1 faults, even if the impedance trajectory becomes unstable. However, the inverter causes several misoperations for zone 2 faults. The reasons are that the impedance trajectories either do not settle within zone 2 due to the inverter becoming unstable or they incorrectly enter zone 1. Moreover, the fault arc resistance and fault location can greatly impact the impedance trajectories obtained when the GFM inverter is connected. Additionally, operating the transmission line above its Surge Impedance Loading (SIL) also increases the risk of making the inverter unstable during faults, causing difficulties with zone 2 protection. When transferring power close to the SIL of the line, it can more reliably become stable but the fault current on the high voltage transmission line tends to be of capacitive nature and thereby making the impedance trajectories settle outside the trip zones.

articleTitle: Practical defence strategy against generic self-learned GOOSE attack
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Cyberattacks across the world have been increasing in frequency and efficacy. As have been highlighted in the recent Ukraine power grid cyberattacks, malicious groups are increasingly selecting infrastructure as a prime target for distributing a nation. A generic object oriented system event (GOOSE) message manipulation attack is described, highlighting the devastating impact that trivially implemented attacks could have. The same attack structure was evaluated when deployed using different vectors: human machine interface (HMI), embedded hardware (i.e supply chain attack) and when implemented by an internal saboteur on a substation. This attack was tested against multiple vendor’s equipment and the results shown. Existing defence strategies are evaluated in this paper exploring and comparing their strengths and weakness. A novel defence mechanism is proposed for securing IEC 61850 GOOSE messages, Trap-bits. This strategy only requires configuration changes to Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) and is compatible with existing substation equipment. Our tests were carried on commercially available substation equipment to secure against the implemented attack, the results were compared to existing methodologies and provide an excellent level of security even when compared to end to end methods.

articleTitle: New time domain distance protection for renewable connected and series compensated transmission lines
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: The nature of today's power transmission networks is getting more complicated and dynamic. Fast, secure, and dependable protection decisions are required for systems that interface with power electronic converters, such as renewable energy resources, series compensated lines, HVDC, FACTS, etc. In these networks, the phasor-based distance protection is prone to reliability problems and has intrinsic speed limitations. In order to satisfy the modern grid protection requirements, we developed a time domain-based protection solution for using incremental quantities of the voltage and currents measured at relay location. The proposed method identified the fault zone by comparing a dynamic restraining quantity which is calculated for the fault zone boundary point with the actual rate of change of current measured at the relay location. The method is implemented in relay platform and validated with both RTDS and field data. The performance of the proposed method is found to be secure, reliable, and fast for lines connected with inverter based renewable resources and series compensated lines.

articleTitle: Protection system design and configuration for extreme weather and emergency grid operating states
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Protection system design and configuration philosophies are usually focused on delivering reliable, sensitive, and selective protection of grid assets. Following a number of major system disturbances in the early to mid-2000s, however, configuration practices evolved to better consider the impact of protection designs on wider grid reliability. In particular, there was a growing recognition of the importance of relay loadability, grid-generator protection coordination, and generator ride-through on the ability of power grids to avoid blackouts in response to major disturbances. This paper will review the recent experience with, and potential future impact of, extreme weather on short circuit fault characteristics, asset failures, and protection performance. The objective of the paper is to identify key protection design and configuration considerations which can be used to reduce the risk of partial or total system collapse. The paper begins by summarising the common forms of extreme weather and how they have impacted grids around the world. Section 2 focuses on the impact of extreme weather on short circuit levels and fault characteristics. These impacts primarily derive from abnormal generation dispatches, generator curtailment and outages, multiple concurrent scheduled and unscheduled line, cable, and transformer outages, and partial and full substation outages. The third section reviews past experience with extreme weather events and protection design philosophy. It gives specific reference to communications system redundancy, circuit breaker failure (CBF) designs considering low circuit breaker gas pressure in extreme cold, and relay microprocessor performance when ambient temperature exceeds device rating. The final section discusses system protection considerations including load-shedding, cascade tripping, power swings, and system defence plans as well as presenting methods for identifying potential protection issues due to extreme weather.

articleTitle: A practical methodology for fault location in transmission lines without line parameter settings and data synchronization
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Reliable fault location for power transmission networks requires line parameters and time synchronized voltage and current measurements from all terminals which may not always be available. In this work, a setting-free fault location methodology using unsynchronized data from the line terminals is proposed. This requires computation of data synchronization error which manifests as a phase angle error between the two terminal phasor measurements. The data synchronization angle is computed using unsynchronized phasors and a design factor related to the line. The design factor can be estimated from a set of synchronized measurements and stored. Upon detecting failure of the data synchronization mechanism, the same can be used to calculate the data synchronization angle between the unsynchronized measurements. The line parameters and subsequently fault location is computed using unsynchronized data and the estimated data synchronization angle. The proposed solution is verified using laboratory experimental and field data and it is found to be accurate.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of DC circuit breakers for future HVDC grids in GB
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper analyses the performance of two different types of Direct Current Circuit Breaker (DCCB) models (hybrid and mechanical) in High Voltage DC (HVDC) networks so that the capabilities and technical specifications of DCCBs can be determined before they are adopted in future multi-terminal HVDC networks in GB. Achieving the 2050 net zero objectives, which will mean linking up to 100 GW of offshore wind to the GB system, necessitates the advancement of HVDC networks beyond the existing point-to-point connections or limited multi-terminal designs. To facilitate the development of multi-terminal HVDC networks, it is necessary to investigate and demonstrate the functionalities of DCCBs. These devices enable the selective and swift disconnection of faulty components, thereby enabling the introduction of more complex topologies and more extensive HVDC networks. The paper briefly outlines the modelling procedures for generic mechanical and hybrid DCCBs. It presents a hypothetical scenario involving a multi-terminal HVDC network, considering the prospective expansion of HVDC connections within the GB transmission system. The evaluation of DCCB performance and specifications is established through numerous simulations conducted in a real-time simulation environment involving different DC fault location and pre-fault power flow simulation scenarios.

articleTitle: Comprehensive monitoring for digital secondary systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Solutions based on digital secondary systems (DSSs), specifically digital process bus, distribute protection and control functions across multiple devices that exchange protection data via communications networks. In such systems, effective monitoring plays a vital role, if properly designed it provides information with respect to the health of the system and complete visibility into the operational status.\Effective monitoring assists in trouble shooting of the system under fault conditions. . Presently DSS designs recurrently prioritize network redundancy to increase system reliability and availability and relegate monitoring capabilities to the background. However, if equally prioritized this would result in optimal performance of the DSS. This paper presents a comprehensive, standards-based monitoring solution for a DSS-based protection system that is operational in a 138 kV substation. It explores the concepts of redundancy and repair, highlighting the challenges created by misconceptions about them and the benefits when they are properly considered. Further, it details the data points necessary for implementing an effective solution and provides practical examples with monitoring screens of the relevant information, which ultimately contributes to increased reliability and availability of a DSS.

articleTitle: AI-assisted design integration of MVDC control and protection
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: A method is presented to assist in the design of control and protection parameters for a Medium Voltage Direct Current (MVDC) system using a Single-Layer Perceptron (SLP) type of Neural Network. Unlike studies that typically verify control and protection parameters separately, in this work different operational scenarios are considered to analyze the joint performance of control and protection design. Then, a neural network is trained to learn the correlation between these parameters and the outcomes of success or failure cases. Tests are conducted using a modular multi-level converter (MMC) topology in an MMC-MVDC point-to-point system. The MMC-HVDC system is modelled in MATLAB/Simulink, and the SLP is developed using the Keras library (integrated with TensorFlow) in Python.

articleTitle: Systems interconnection and voltage stability protection schemes increase power transfer limits and prevent regional blackouts at Panama's transmission system
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Panama’s transmission system has geographical and infrastructure constraints that make it very susceptible to different contingencies. These contingencies have led to major blackouts that have affected loads in Panama and the Central American transmission system in recent years. ETESA – CND developed a special protection scheme that takes remedial actions to increase reliability and power transfer limits of the Central American regional system to allow for the most economical operation. Excess generation in the Panama system and Central American interconnection overload could be steady state or transient conditions caused by uncontrolled and major loss of load due to fault induced slow voltage recovery (FIDVR), events such as N-2 contingencies, load shedding schemes, by oscillations caused by failures with long clearing times, or various other reasons. This paper presents the principal challenges found during power system studies and the remedial action solutions implemented. Schemes require accurate and simultaneous measurement of the total power flow at the interconnection link composed by three transmission lines during transient conditions. Synchrophasors measurements (PMUs) and PMU high speed phasor concentration technologies (PDCs) are applied for synchronous measurement and used to make generation-shedding decisions. The proposed solution combines different schemes and logics in order to be effective for several different contingencies and operating conditions. Very fast generation-shedding actions are preferred, but pre-armed, contingency-based schemes cannot be applied for uncontrolled loss of load due to FIDVR, because there is no single location to detect contingency. The scheme needs to respond to power flow measurements after the event. Two response-based schemes are described, one uses the total power flow in the three interconnection lines to make tripping decisions during slower evolution events, while the other calculates the rate-of-change of power at the interconnection link to accelerate the protection. Generation-shedding algorithms perform a real-time selection among multiple generation plants to optimize amount to shed and automatically changes selection both after dispatch changes, and after initial operation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of travelling wave protection performance in converter-dominated networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study to investigate the travelling wave protection performance in network s with high penetration of Converter-Based Resources (CBRs). Representative network models are developed in the sub-step environment of the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) and realistic Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) tests are conducted on a pair of travelling wave relays (TWRs) to emulate realistic system and fault scenarios. The studies have been conducted in two stages: firstly, systematic tests with a total number of 300 cases have been conducted to have a high-level assessment of TWRs’ performance under different fault conditions, e.g. varied fault types, fault positions, Fault Inception Angles (FIAs), and fault resistances; and secondly, detailed investigation has been conducted on selected and representative cases to understand the impact of various factors, e.g. the line-end transformer, system fault levels, converter controls and external faults, on the protection performance. Based on the test results and analysis, it was found that the performance of the TWR is largely unaffected by the variation of system fault levels and converter control strategies, but the connection of the line-end transformer and the low FIAs present challenges for the healthy operation of TWRs in some conditions. Although the tests were conducted for a pair of specific commercially available TWRs, the results have been analysed in a generic manner, so the findings will not only facilitate understanding the benefits/limitations of travelling wave protection in the network with high amounts of CBRs, but also provide a valuable reference for system operators to select the protection solutions in the future.

articleTitle: Modified empirical arc model for simulating HVdc open conductor faults
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: One fault that has hitherto not widely been investigated is the open circuiting of an HVdc conductor, as its occurrence is relatively rare. Using electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation, this paper addresses the void in HVdc fault analysis by giving useful insight into the impact of HVdc open conductor faults on current and voltage transients. In order to simulate the resulting series arc between falling HVdc conductors, the Schavemaker model, a well-known empirical model, is adapted by introducing the dynamics of varying arc length. The modified Schavemaker arc model is implemented in PSCAD/ EMTDC. This study analyzes the impact of each parameter of the Schavemaker arc model on the arc conductance variation during an open conductor fault. This study shows that the arc time constant is the most influential parameter on the arc conductance variation while the time-varying reference arc voltage and arc cooling power introduces the effect of variable arc lengths to the Schawmaker model.

articleTitle: Test bench development for functional testing of DC protection relays
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: HVDC systems that interconnect large generation and load centres are expected to facilitate the massive expansion of offshore wind energy. These HVDC systems combine vendor-specific technical designs and operation concepts. The successful operation of these HVDC systems requires well-defined functional specifications and test procedures for all the components of the protection system. To validate the performance of DC protection relays, a test bench for DC relays is necessary. However, existing requirements for DC relay tests are unclear, and no standardized procedures exist to validate the functionality of HVDC protection. Currently, real-time simulation is the most advanced testing method available, but it has accuracy limitations for high bandwidth testing, and its practicality and cost-effectiveness can vary based on the application. This paper presents a novel design of a DC protection relay test bench and discusses key considerations and hardware specifications for a suitable test bench. The presented test bench meets future testing requirements and includes high sample rates, accurate models, and necessary automation controls. Finally, several case studies are presented to demonstrate the practical implementations and test limitations of the test bench.

articleTitle: Power-swing detection logic for systems with low inertia
publicationTitle: 17th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP 2024)
abstract: Distance protection elements face security problems during power-swing conditions because the swelling power may cause the apparent impedance to encroach on the element operating characteristics. To address this problem, line distance protective relays include a power-swing blocking logic to secure their distance elements during power swings. Avoiding undesired line tripping keeps the transmission network intact and gives the system time to stabilize through inherent transient stability margins and dedicated transient stability schemes, including load and generation shedding, power system stabilizers, and remedial action schemes. From the protection perspective, however, assertion of the power-swing blocking logic hurts protection dependability during power-swing conditions. Symmetrical faults that cannot be detected by using sequence directional elements in a pilot protection scheme are of particular concern.
